justifications.functional_suitability: Customer/Broker Portal (R-01), Adjuster Workstation and BFF (R-02), and Claim Migration Manager plus Claim Routing & Feature Flag Component (R-03) exist. Gaps: the Migration Manager's target 'Migration Controller API' is undefined, and portal-to-domain flows and per-claim-type migration are thin.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Read Model & Cache Store replica, Read-Model Cache Manager, asynchronous Azure Service Bus via Integration Worker, SSE sync, PgBouncer, and Redis caching directly target the 2 s versus 5 s latency. No explicit load-test or autoscaling mechanism, and the cache invalidation strategy is unclear.
justifications.compatibility: Integration Worker with Transformation Engine, ACL Gateway, MFT, and Entra ID via OIDC address interoperability. Gaps: the ACL Gateway is modelled inconsistently (external system versus component), the mainframe interface is vague, and the batch window and one-change-per-quarter constraint are unaddressed.
justifications.usability: Distinct channels exist for Policyholders and Brokers (Customer/Broker Portal), Adjusters (Adjuster Workstation with Claims Dashboard and SSE updates), and admins (Admin Portal). Brokers share one portal with customers, and there is no UX or accessibility mechanism or status feedback detail.
justifications.reliability: Outbox/Retry Dispatcher, Idempotency & Audit Manager, Polly Circuit Breaker Policy Manager, APIM Circuit Breaker & Retry Engine, Feature/Kill-Switch, and PostgreSQL high availability address R-04 and R-06. Gaps: no explicit reconciliation, DR or backup, and the Integration Worker and APIM contain inconsistent flows.
justifications.security: Entra ID SSO via OIDC, APIM Token Validator, rate limiting, TLS everywhere, pgaudit Audit & Compliance Log Store, Integration Audit Logger, and Private Link/VPN ingress. Gaps: no secrets management, no explicit RBAC enforcement at services, and the customer authentication path is unclear.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container split (BFF, Core Claims Domain, Integration Worker, Migration Manager), ACL isolation of legacy, DDD, MediatR, and Feature Flag routing. Gaps: the Operational Data Store is duplicated as a component, the Migration Manager has a single component, and relationships are inconsistent with the model.
justifications.portability: Azure Container Apps, PostgreSQL, OpenTelemetry, and gRPC give some portability, and a hybrid on-prem/Azure link exists via ExpressRoute and MFT. Heavy use of Azure-managed services (APIM, Service Bus, Application Insights) causes lock-in, and no IaC or containerization strategy is explicit.

sensitivity_points: Cache miss path still hits 5 s mainframe
tradeoffs: Read-model caching improves latency but risks stale claim data
PERF-01.justification: A BFF read-model cache and read replica plus async ACL can plausibly meet 2 s. But cache population, invalidation and cold-miss behaviour are unspecified, and the Legacy Integration Gateway is a possible synchronous path.

sensitivity_points: Batch window scheduling of dispatch to mainframe
Service Bus queue depth during spikes
tradeoffs: Queue buffering absorbs peaks but delays mainframe sync
PERF-02.justification: Async Service Bus decoupling and an outbox buffer the 5x peak. But no explicit mechanism keeps the Integration Worker from pushing load into the batch window, and autoscaling is not described.

sensitivity_points: Outbox durability and replay ordering after window
Circuit breaker thresholds during planned downtime
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency with mainframe in exchange for continued intake
AVAIL-01.justification: Submissions are persisted in the platform's own store, with outbox, retry and circuit breaker forwarding later through durable Service Bus. This fits the scenario well. A scheduled-window-aware release is not explicit.

sensitivity_points: Idempotency keys must be honoured by the mainframe side
Reconciliation process is not explicitly modelled
AVAIL-02.justification: The idempotency manager, outbox with retry, audit logging and migration metadata prevent loss and duplicates. However, there is no explicit reconciliation component and mainframe-side dedup is not shown, so the half-way failure is only partly covered.

sensitivity_points: Mainframe interface change count per quarter
tradeoffs: Routing flexibility adds flag complexity and dual-path testing
MOD-01.justification: Feature-flag routing, a kill-switch, a migration manager and an ACL transformation engine support per-type migration and quick switch-back. The admin portal component is thin, with a dangling Migration Controller API, and data back-sync on rollback is unspecified.

sensitivity_points: Data ownership switch from mainframe to PostgreSQL
ACL removal must not leak into UIs
tradeoffs: ACL indirection costs complexity but isolates UIs from the legacy
MOD-02.justification: UIs talk only to the BFF and the domain, which are isolated from the mainframe behind the ACL, so UIs stay unchanged. The PostgreSQL store can become the system of record. A final data migration and cutover plan is not shown.

tradeoffs: Central gateway authorization simplifies checks but is coarse-grained
SEC-01.justification: Token validation and audit logging exist, but no component enforces per-broker data-level authorization on claims or records denied attempts. Nothing guards access in the mainframe. Role checks alone would not stop cross-broker access.

sensitivity_points: Token and session lifetime versus 15 minute revocation
Mainframe credential mapping to AD not shown
tradeoffs: Short token lifetimes improve revocation but increase re-authentication load
SEC-02.justification: Entra ID SSO centralizes revocation for the new platform. But token lifetime and session caching are unspecified, and nothing addresses how mainframe access is removed within 15 minutes, so the both-systems requirement is unmet.
